findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value, so illegal shard states (e.g. "deleted", null, "sent" without is_sent=true) are representable and cannot be rejected at compile time.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set status to an invalid value, leaving the shard in a semantically inconsistent state that no type-level invariant prevents.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a domain enum `pub enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }` and make status an owned enum value.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive boolean flag that cannot enforce lifecycle ordering. Nothing prevents calling mark_sent on an unvalidated shard, or setting is_validated without transitioning status.
findings.failure_mode: Shard can transition through invalid state sequences (e.g. sent without being validated, or validated then sent then marked validated again), violating the domain workflow invariant.
findings.fix: Replace `is_validated: bool` with a typestate enum or integrate into the ShardStatus enum so that validation is a prerequisite of the Sent state, enforced by the type system.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is redundant with status == "sent" and creates dual-mutation sources. mark_sent sets both status and is_sent but nothing enforces they stay in sync.
findings.failure_mode: A caller could manually set is_sent to true while leaving status as "pending", creating an inconsistent observable state that breaks downstream logic depending on either field.
findings.fix: Remove `is_sent: bool` entirely. Derive sent-ness from the ShardStatus enum variant. If a separate flag is needed, make it a derived accessor (`fn is_sent(&self) -> bool`) computed from status.

findings.problem: All data and logic is public mutable state with no functional core. mark_sent mutates in place and there is no separation between pure domain calculations and imperative shell. No typed domain constructors validate invariants at construction time.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct ShardWorkflow with any combination of fields, bypassing all invariants. No parsing-at-boundary, no trusted-by-construction data, no pure core to test independently.
findings.fix: Make the struct fields private. Provide a fallible constructor that validates invariants. Split mark_sent into a pure domain function `fn mark_sent(status: ShardStatus) -> Result<ShardStatus, TransitionError>` and keep mutation in an imperative shell layer.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. There is no validation that the id matches expected format, length, or uniqueness rules.
findings.failure_mode: Empty, malformed, or duplicate shard IDs can be stored and cause silent data corruption or lookup failures downstream.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `pub struct ShardId(String)` with a constructor that validates format/length constraints, replacing the raw String field.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> uses a raw u64 without a domain newtype, making it indistinguishable from other epoch values.
findings.failure_mode: Confusion between sent_at_epoch_ms and other timestamp fields enables incorrect comparisons, logging, or arithmetic on the wrong temporal value.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `SentAtEpochMs(u64)` with Display/Copy impl, replacing the raw Option<u64>.

residual_risk: The struct represents illegal states freely (any string status, unsynchronized bool flags, no validation). mark_sent is an in-place mutation with no domain validation or typestate enforcement. Without enum-based status, typestate lifecycle, private fields, and a pure domain core, all invariants are runtime-enforced at best and unverifiable without integration tests.
